notes: WHO RUNS IT: Mississippi's All-State choirs are split between two bodies, and this was verified in the official MSMEA/MHSAA Senior High Choral Division Informational Manual. The HIGH SCHOOL All-State Honor Choirs (SATB, Treble, and Show Choir) are 'organized and governed by the MS ACDA Executive Board' — Mississippi ACDA, not the MEA. The JUNIOR HIGH All-State Honor Choirs (SATB, Treble, Show Choir) and the ELEMENTARY All-State Honor Choir are MMEA (Mississippi Music Educators Association) events. All of them rehearse and perform together at the joint MMEA / MS ACDA State Conference, all of them audition through the same Opus Event system, and all of them appear on a single shared repertoire list and a single shared timeline, which is why they are recorded here as one state entry. MHSAA (Mississippi High School Activities Association) sanctions the events and hosts the choral division manual but does not run the honor choirs. SEASON LABELING: Mississippi labels this cycle by the calendar year of the conference — the timeline PDF is headed '2026 MMEA•ACDA ALL-STATE CONFERENCE NOV 16-18' and the repertoire spreadsheet is titled '2026 All-State Honor Choir Rep. List'. Those are the CURRENT cycle, not prior-year data: auditions run August 2026 and the conference is November 16-18, 2026, i.e. the 2026-27 school year, and msacda.org stamps its All-State Honor Choirs block 'Updated July 28, 2026'. Season is therefore recorded as 2026-27 while Mississippi's own label is '2026'. DATE CAVEAT: the timeline PDF prints month and day only, with no year beside each milestone; the year 2026 is taken from the document's own title and is consistent with the November 16-18, 2026 conference date confirmed on msacda.org. AGE OF SUPPORTING DOCS: the audition-process and sight-reading rules below come from the 2025-2026 edition of the MSMEA HS Choral Division Manual, which was still the newest posted on misshsaa.com at retrieval (MHSAA had posted a 2026-27 general Handbook but no 2026-27 choral division manual). Those rules are standing procedure rather than dated items, but they have not been reconfirmed against a 2026-27 manual. Note also that the 2025-26 manual says the state conference is 'typically in mid to late January', while both MMEA and MS ACDA now advertise November 16-18, 2026, with MSACDA flagging it as a 'New Date' — the November date is the one used here.

organization.name: Mississippi American Choral Directors Association
organization.description: MS ACDA organizes and governs Mississippi's high school All-State Honor Choirs — the All-State SATB Honor Choir, the All-State Treble Honor Choir, and the All-State Honor Show Choir — through its Executive Board. Rehearsals and concerts take place in conjunction with the annual joint MMEA / MS ACDA State Conference. The junior high and elementary All-State Honor Choirs on the same timeline are run by the Mississippi Music Educators Association (MMEA/MSMEA).

programs.name: MS ACDA All-State SATB Honor Choir
programs.description: An enriching choral experience for outstanding high school age vocal students statewide, organized and governed by the MS ACDA Executive Board. Only the highest-scoring auditions are selected to work with nationally recognized conductors. Rehearsals and the concert take place in conjunction with the annual MMEA / MS ACDA State Conference. Mississippi ACDA lists Jordan Durham of Starkville High School as the All-State SATB Honor Choir chair.

requirements.title: Director must be a current MS ACDA member and must register for the conference
requirements.description: The choral director must be a current member of MS ACDA for their students to participate in auditions, and must register for the conference if any of their students are accepted into an honor choir. Because rehearsals and concerts take place in conjunction with the State Conference, a sponsoring MS ACDA member must be registered for the conference to enable honor choir participation.

requirements.title: Two specified audition pieces from the All-State repertoire list
requirements.description: Students learn several selections from the released repertoire list; two of those selections are designated as the audition pieces, and students sing excerpts from both at the audition.

requirements.title: Audition scoring — 444 points maximum
requirements.description: The two audition pieces are worth 100 points each, for 200 points. Sight-reading is worth an additional 22 points, making it 10% of the total audition score. There are two judges for each student, resulting in a maximum score of 444 points.

requirements.title: Mississippi All-State sight-reading — one eight-measure exercise
requirements.description: One eight-measure exercise, administered from a recorded prompt available on msacda.org, sung in the same audition room immediately after the excerpts. Sopranos and tenors read in G; altos and basses read in D. Students may sing or hum along with the tonal orientation on the recording but may not sing during the 45-second study period. All exercises start on the tonic. Tempo is set at quarter note = 60; students may sing faster but not slower. The exercise may be sung with solfege, numbers, or a neutral syllable. One restart is allowed — if it is used after a completed first reading, only the second reading is scored; the starting pitch may be replayed but no additional study time is given. Exercises include phrase markings and expressive symbols.

requirements.title: Sight-reading content limits and scoring
requirements.description: Rhythmic components: whole, half, quarter, two eighths, dotted half, and dotted quarter/eighth notes; half and quarter rests. Melodic components: skips of a third in the I chord (D-M, M-D, M-S, S-M), the perfect fifth skip (D-S, S-D), and skips of a third in the V chord (S-T, T-S, T-R, R-T). Scoring out of 22: one point per measure with correct rhythm, one point per measure with correct pitch, up to two points for a steady beat, up to two points for intonation and maintaining the tonal center, and up to two points for observing phrasing and dynamic indications.

requirements.title: Auditions submitted through Opus Event
requirements.description: Auditions are submitted through Opus Event, a web-based system. The audition fee must be marked paid before an audition can be submitted.

requirements.title: Quartet audition with recorded accompaniment, plus sight-reading
